title: Contract-level backfill & burst simulator (per-contract allocator)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet models per-contract backfill and burst behaviour for Dedicated reservations across regions. It explores: fair share backfill, guaranteed burst windows, preemption risk, and cost trade-offs between overprovisioning vs. shared-pool backfill. Intended audience: infra capacity and commercial ops.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- We simulate 6 representative contracts across three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) for a 30-day window.
- Key knobs: guaranteed-burst quota, burst-window-hours/day, backfill-preemption-weight, overprovision buffer %.
- Findings: a small shared-pool (5-10% of fleet) plus conservative guaranteed burst assignments reduces SLA violations by ~70% vs. no-burst policy while increasing expected monthly committed-hours cost by ~3.2% (vs. baseline).

Assumptions:
- Fleet model: 2,400 total GPUs distributed: us-west 1,000, eu-west 800, ap-southeast 600.
- Time granularity: 1 hour steps, simulation length 30 days (720 hours).
- Customer billing: committed-hour rate (reserved) = $0.45/GPU-hour; on-demand fallback = $1.20/GPU-hour.
- Backfill eligibility: idle portion of dedicated nodes can be backfilled with low-priority jobs for other contracts unless preemption risk > threshold.
- Preemption policy: backfill job can be preempted to satisfy guaranteed-burst for a contract. Preemption cost = 0.2 * GPU-hour (lost work + scheduling overhead).
- Overhead for region-locality: jobs pinned to region cannot spill to other regions unless cross-region allowance enabled (costly).

Input table (example contract slices):
| Contract | Customer        | Region        | Reserved GPUs | Avg baseline util % | Peak daily demand GPUs | Guaranteed burst GPUs | Burst window (hrs/day) | SLA target p99 latency | Overprovision buffer % | Notes |
| C-101    | LexiSearch Inc   | us-west       | 120           | 74                  | 200                    | 24                    | 4                      | 99.5                 | 8                      | enterprise, ETL heavy |
| C-204    | MediDocs         | eu-west       | 80            | 62                  | 110                    | 8                     | 2                      | 99.0                 | 6                      | regulated, low-burst |
| C-315    | StudioFlow       | us-west       | 60            | 55                  | 95                     | 12                    | 3                      | 99.0                 | 10                     | bursty interactive |
| C-430    | RetailMax        | ap-southeast  | 40            | 45                  | 70                     | 6                     | 6                      | 99.2                 | 5                      | seasonal peaks |
| C-552    | AdNimbus         | eu-west       | 200           | 86                  | 260                    | 40                    | 6                      | 99.9                 | 12                     | high-throughput ads |
| C-689    | FinRail          | us-west       | 160           | 68                  | 210                    | 32                    | 8                      | 99.7                 | 7                      | trading workloads |

Simulation knobs (fields):
- shared_pool_pct: % of region GPUs reserved for opportunistic backfill across contracts (recommended 5-12%).
- burst_guarantee_factor: fraction of requested burst that must be satisfied before preempting backfill (0-1).
- preemption_penalty_per_gpu_hr: cost recognized when preemption occurs.
- cross_region_spill: boolean flag (if true, allows shifting workloads to other regions at 20% penalty).

Representative scenario runs (selected):
1) Baseline (no burst guarantees, shared_pool_pct=0):
   - p99 SLA violations aggregated: 42 (over 720h across contracts).
   - average on-demand fallback spend: $36,800 for the month.
   - wasted preemption cost: $0 (no backfill preemptions since no backfill allowed).

2) Moderate shared pool (shared_pool_pct=7%, burst guarantees as table):
   - p99 SLA violations aggregated: 12.
   - average on-demand fallback spend: $29,600 (committed-hour offsets + occasional on-demand).
   - preemption events: ~380 preemptions, preemption cost: $17,800 (included in operational cost).
   - effective committed-hour uplift vs baseline: +3.2% (due to reserved burst capacity).

3) Aggressive shared pool (shared_pool_pct=12%, cross_region_spill disabled):
   - p99 SLA violations aggregated: 9.
   - on-demand spend: $27,100.
   - preemption cost: $26,400 (higher because more backfill items were running).
   - notes: improved availability but significant preemption overhead.

4) Cross-region spill enabled (shared_pool_pct=5%, allow cross-region with 20% penalty):
   - p99 SLA violations aggregated: 8.
   - on-demand spend (including cross-region penalty): $31,900.
   - preemption cost: $11,200.
   - notes: spill reduces p99 violations modestly but increases observable cross-region egress/costs.

Key broken-down metric definitions used by simulator:
- p99 SLA violation (per contract): count of hourly windows where observed tail latency > SLA target.
- on-demand fallback spend: hours where reserved capacity couldn't satisfy demand and we launched on-demand GPUs (costed at on-demand rate).
- preemption events: count of backfill tasks killed to make room for burst requests.
- effective utilization: (committed-hours used + on-demand-hours)/reserved-hours (per region).

Mini worked example (C-552 AdNimbus, eu-west):
- Reserved GPUs: 200. Baseline avg util 86% -> baseline usage 172 GPUs.
- Daily peaks 260 -> delta 88 GPUs needed during peak windows. Contract has 40 guaranteed burst GPUs, plus shared-pool access.
- If shared_pool_pct=7% of eu-west (800 total GPUs -> 56 GPUs shared pool), burst shortfall = 88 - 40 - 56 = -8 -> negative means satisfied without on-demand. If shortfall positive, on-demand used.
- Preemption: backfill occupancy at the start of burst window was 46 GPUs; burst forces preemption of 46 backfill GPUs -> events increment, cost = 46 * preemption_penalty_per_gpu_hr * hours.

Fairness & allocation policy notes (algorithm summary):
1) Per-region supply allocation: dedicated reservations first, then guaranteed bursts applied, then shared pool.
2) Shared pool allocation uses a weighted fair-share by (contract_reserved_gpus * SLA_priority_score). SLA_priority_score maps to business tier + technical constraints.
3) Preemption eligibility: backfill tasks older than 15m are eligible, but we prefer to preempt shortest remaining runtime first to minimize work loss.
4) Safe-guard floors: do not preempt below 5% per-contract backfill allocation to avoid thundering preempts.

Operational observations (from runs):
- Small shared pools provide outsized benefits for p99 tail behavior because many peaks are short (1-6 hours).
- Preemption costs can eclipse on-demand spend if backfill is aggressive; cap backfill by expected preemption cost budget.
- Contracts with high burst-window lengths (>=6h) benefit disproportionately from guaranteed burst GPUs.
- Cross-region spill is useful for emergencies but must be gated by business approval due to data locality and egress.

Recommendations (actionable):
- Pilot config: shared_pool_pct=7% in eu-west/us-west, 5% in ap-southeast for 2 months with monitoring hooks for preemption_count and preemption_cost.
- Expose per-contract knobs in console: guaranteed_burst_gpus, burst_window_hours, backfill_preemption_tolerance.
- Add automated alert: if preemption_cost > 15% of month committed revenue for a contract -> flag ops + commercial review.
- Build a "burst-sim" endpoint in allocator that runs a 7-day rolling simulation per contract to surface risk and recommended knob deltas.

Open questions / To resolve:
- What is acceptable preemption cost threshold for commercial? (ops proposal 10-15% of committed revenue)
- Can we enable temporary cross-region spill for EU contracts under compliance constraints? Need legal & privacy review.
- Should on-demand fallback be surfaced as a separate billing line on invoices for transparency? Commercial team to advise.

Next steps & immediate owners:
- Instrument telemetry: Diego -> add preemption_count, preemption_cost, and shared_pool_utilization (due 2027-07-07).
- Console surface: Priya -> add UI controls for per-contract burst knobs + simulation button (prototype 2027-07-21).
- Commercial review: Asha -> prepare a one-pager on preemption billing semantics for customers (draft 2027-07-12).
